learningObjective: Explain what continuous (iteration-level) batching is and why it improves throughput over static batching for LLM serving.
stem: Continuous batching (also called iteration-level batching, as introduced by Orca and used by vLLM) is compared to static request-level batching. Which description of its main mechanism and benefit is correct?

options.text: Continuous batching runs each request on its own dedicated CUDA stream so that per-request scheduling decisions do not serialize across the batch; the throughput win comes from independent execution paths per request.

Continuous batching packs all decode requests together every step but forbids adding new requests until every existing request has produced the same number of tokens; this uniform-progress requirement preserves batching efficiency at the cost of latency.

Continuous batching converts autoregressive decode into a single-pass generation by predicting all output tokens simultaneously with a non-autoregressive draft model; the primary win is bypassing the sequential decode dependency.

At every model-forward iteration the scheduler builds a batch from currently-active requests: new requests can join and finished requests can leave between iterations without waiting for the whole batch to complete. This keeps the GPU utilized despite variable-length outputs.

explanation: Continuous (iteration-level) batching, as introduced by Orca and implemented in vLLM, rebuilds the batch at the granularity of a single model-forward iteration. New requests can join mid-flight and finished ones leave immediately, avoiding the head-of-line blocking of static batching where the whole batch waits for the longest request. This dramatically improves GPU utilization for workloads with variable-length outputs.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: iteration-level batching runs one shared model forward per iteration; per-request streams are irrelevant.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: uniform progress is not required; that would defeat the whole point.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: describes non-autoregressive generation, not continuous batching.

assumptions: Requests share the same model but can have different sequence lengths and prompt positions.
The scheduler operates at the model-forward-iteration granularity.
nonImplications: Does not imply per-token quality changes; the same math runs.
Does not imply zero overhead; batch composition and KV cache management have some cost.

distractorRationales.A: Confuses batching granularity with stream parallelism.

performanceClaim.scope: Continuous batching for variable-length LLM generation
